rows.pin_name: Jerusalem — Western Wall Tunnels / Temple Mount Western Wall
rows.rule_line: Dress modestly and do not bring your own Torah scroll to the Western Wall plaza. On the Sabbath and Jewish holidays, photos and electronic devices are not allowed. Check before you go.
rows.source_name: Western Wall Heritage Foundation — Guidelines for Behavior at the Western Wall
rows.note: WWHF official 'Respectful Conduct' list (dress appropriately; no Torah scrolls brought into the plaza; on Sabbath/holidays no electronic devices or pictures). Main plaza prayer is gender-separated; an egalitarian platform sits south of the Mughrabi Bridge (State 2023 IRF).

rows.pin_name: Jerusalem — Western Wall Tunnels / Temple Mount Western Wall
rows.rule_line: Non-Muslims may visit the Temple Mount (Haram al-Sharif) only through the Mughrabi Gate at set hours and may not enter the Dome of the Rock or al-Aqsa Mosque. Non-Muslim prayer is officially barred under the long-standing status quo, and police screen visitors for religious items, but enforcement has shifted in recent years. Check before you go.
rows.source_name: U.S. Department of State — 2023 Report on International Religious Freedom: West Bank and Gaza (covers East Jerusalem)
rows.note: Second row for this pin: the Mughrabi Gate (only non-Muslim entrance) is reached from the Western Wall plaza. State's 2023 IRF report (latest published; covers calendar 2023): Israel backs the status quo allowing non-Muslim visitors but prohibiting non-Islamic worship; police control the Mughrabi Gate and admit visitors during set hours; the Waqf keeps non-Muslims out of the Dome of the Rock and al-Aqsa; police screen non-Muslims for religious articles; the report also records Jewish prayer on the site and says police generally allowed discreet non-Muslim prayer. Site has also closed to non-Muslims in the last 10 days of Ramadan. Contested: Israeli government, Jordan/Waqf and Temple Mount groups describe the rules differently; wording kept neutral.

rows.rule_line: Hebron is split into a Palestinian Authority zone (H1) and a zone under Israeli military control (H2) that includes the Cave of the Patriarchs (Ibrahimi Mosque). At the Cave, Jews and Muslims pray in separate sections, and the army closes it to each faith on about 10 of the other faith's holidays a year. Check before you go.
rows.source_name: U.S. Department of State — 2023 Report on International Religious Freedom: West Bank and Gaza (covers East Jerusalem)
rows.note: State 2023 IRF: H1/H2 split; IDF controls access to the Ibrahimi Mosque/Tomb of the Patriarchs, restricts Muslim access ~10 days on Jewish holidays and Jewish access ~10 days on Islamic holidays, Muslims use one entry point with metal detectors; physical separation since 1994. Pin is Tel Rumeida, a short walk from the Cave; the source does not name Tel Rumeida, so the line is phrased at city level. Palestinian and Israeli officials dispute control of the site.

rows.rule_line: Israeli citizens, including dual U.S.-Israeli citizens, are generally barred by Israel from entering Area A of the West Bank, which includes Jericho. Check before you go.
rows.source_name: U.S. Department of State — Country Information: Israel, the West Bank and Gaza
rows.note: State Israel/WB/Gaza country page (last updated 2025-03-28): Israeli citizens 'are generally prohibited from traveling to parts of the West Bank under PA control (Area A), to include Bethlehem and Jericho'; same page says Israel treats dual U.S.-Israeli citizens as Israeli citizens. State's 2023 IRF report adds that large Israeli road signs warn Israelis entry is illegal, and that some Israeli citizens still visit privately. Applies to Israeli citizens only, not other visitors.

rows.pin_name: Rome — Vatican Necropolis / St. Peter’s tomb tradition
rows.rule_line: Visits to the Vatican Necropolis are by advance booking only, in small guided groups, and children under 10 are not admitted. Shoulders and knees must be covered, and photos and video are not allowed inside. Check before you go.
rows.source_name: Papal Basilica of Saint Peter (Fabbrica di San Pietro) — Vatican Necropolis FAQ
rows.note: Official Fabbrica di San Pietro FAQ: mandatory advance booking, groups of max 12 with an authorized guide, no children under 10, shoulders and knees covered, no photography/video; closed Sundays and Vatican holidays.

rows.pin_name: Mount Ararat / Doğubayazıt region (flood-tradition archaeology caution row)
rows.rule_line: Mount Ararat is a special military zone, and you must get access permission from a Turkish embassy or consulate before you arrive in Turkey. Check before you go.
rows.source_name: U.S. Department of State — Country Information: Turkey
rows.note: State Turkey country page (last updated 2026-06-11): 'Mount Ararat, in Agri province, is a special military zone, and access permission must be obtained before coming to Turkey from a Turkish Embassy or Consulate.'

rows.rule_line: Carchemish (Karkamış) sits on the Turkey–Syria border, where Turkish security forces control access. Do not photograph or film military activity or try to enter military sites. Check before you go.
rows.source_name: U.S. Department of State — Country Information: Turkey
rows.note: State Turkey page: 'Turkish security forces control access to ... the entire Turkey-Syria border' and 'Do not photograph or video Turkish military operations or attempt to enter military installations anywhere in Turkey.' The site's archaeological park is open; how access works on the day is not stated by an official source we found.

rows.rule_line: Egypt requires permission and a set route from Military Intelligence and the Tourist Police to visit areas near the Israel border or off paved roads in Sinai, which likely covers this remote site. Check before you go.
rows.source_name: U.S. Department of State — Country Information: Egypt
rows.note: State Egypt page (last updated 2025-08-11): travelers must get permission and a travel route from Egyptian Military Intelligence and the Tourist Police to access borders with Israel and parts of Sinai off paved roads; all border areas are under military control. Kuntillet Ajrud is a remote NE Sinai site near the Israel border; the page does not name it. North/Middle Sinai is also a State 'avoid' area.

rows.rule_line: Saudi rules do not allow the public display of non-Muslim religious items such as crosses or Bibles. Visitors should cover shoulders and knees, and photos of local people, especially women, need clear consent. Check before you go.
rows.source_name: U.S. Department of State — Country Information: Saudi Arabia
rows.note: State Saudi Arabia page (last updated 2026-05-21), Local Laws: public display of non-Islamic religious articles such as crosses and Bibles not permitted; tourists expected to cover shoulders and knees; never photograph women without consent; no photos of military/government sites. Nationwide.

rows.rule_line: Iranian law requires a government dress code for all visitors; women must cover their hair, arms, and legs. Taking photos near military or government sites is strictly banned. Check before you go.
rows.source_name: U.S. Department of State — Country Information: Iran
rows.note: State Iran country page (last updated 2025-12-11), Local Laws. Nationwide rule, applies at this site. Iran is Level 4 Do Not Travel.

rows.pin_name: Soleb Temple — Shasu of Yhwȝ inscription
rows.rule_line: Sudan requires a travel permit from the Ministry of Tourism for trips outside greater Khartoum, and taking photos needs a separate government permit. Check before you go.
rows.source_name: U.S. Department of State — Country Information: Sudan
rows.note: State Sudan page (last updated 2025-11-12): permit from the Ministry of Tourism required outside greater Khartoum; photography requires a permit from the External Information Centre. Sudan is Level 4 (armed conflict); whether the permit offices are working is unclear, so mixed.

rows.rule_line: Salamis is in the Turkish Cypriot-administered north, so cross the UN buffer zone only at an official crossing point and show your passport. Never photograph military sites. Check before you go.
rows.source_name: U.S. Department of State — Country Information: Cyprus
rows.note: State Cyprus page (last updated 2026-08-13): do not enter the UN buffer zone except at designated crossing points; cross with a valid U.S. passport at recognized checkpoints; never photograph military installations; police on both sides enforce this.
